stories.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, an open loop transformer that runs on a laptop
stories.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open looped transformer that reruns some layers per token to reason longer without extra text. It matches Qwen3.8 27B on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index at about six times lower cost.
stories.more: Inkling 2 Mini is an open looped transformer released by Thinking Machines. It runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token, letting it reason internally for longer instead of generating extra text. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, it ties with Qwen3.8 27B while costing roughly six times less to run. The model is described as able to run on a laptop. It is not stated how its weights are licensed beyond being described as open.

stories.title: Bytedance's open model Axion 1.0 argues most AI training phases are unnecessary
stories.summary: Bytedance and several US universities released Axion 1.0, an open AI agent that rivals top OpenAI and Anthropic models on benchmarks after only three training phases, crediting curated data rather than more training steps.
stories.more: Bytedance, working with several US universities, introduced Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks. The team reached that result after just three training phases, far fewer than typical. They attribute the gains to carefully curated training data rather than additional training steps. The model, its training data, and its code are all freely available. It is not stated which specific benchmarks were used for the comparison.

stories.title: Anthropic claims Claude proved Riemann hypothesis; Stanford publishes rival human proof
stories.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude produced a Lean-formalized proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Stanford then published a rival all-human proof hours later, and mathematicians are now verifying both.
stories.more: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a problem that has been open for 167 years. The proof is formalized in the Lean theorem-proving language and spans more than 250,000 pages. Just hours after that claim, a separate team of Stanford researchers published their own proof of the same hypothesis, produced entirely by humans. Mathematicians are now independently checking both proofs to see whether either one actually holds up. It is not yet known whether either proof will be confirmed correct.

stories.title: US tech stocks post worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts mount
stories.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell into a bear market after its worst weekly loss since the Covid-19 crash. Nvidia dropped 14% amid an SEC accounting review, and Anthropic gave back most of its gains a day after its IPO.
stories.more: The Nasdaq 100 slipped into a bear market after suffering its worst weekly loss since the Covid-19 crisis. Nvidia shares plunged 14 percent as the SEC reviews its accounting practices. Anthropic lost nearly all of its gains a day after what was described as a record IPO. The sell-off is attributed to a mix of AI doubts, scandals, rising interest rates, and political headwinds hitting already overheated valuations. It is not stated how long the SEC review is expected to take.
